summary.text: Jordan Teuscher is a Republican member of the Utah House of Representatives for District 44, where he has served since 2021, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026, general election.
An attorney, he has led international legal-reform work and, according to his 2020 Ballotpedia survey, works for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

paragraphs.text: Teuscher was born in Salt Lake City and earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University in 2007 and a J.D. from BYU's J. Reuben Clark Law School in 2012.

His career has included work as an attorney, as executive director of the Leavitt Institute for International Development directing legal reform work in eastern Europe and Africa, and with the International Center for Law and Religion Studies.
In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, he said he grew up in South Jordan, Utah, and worked after law school for a firm specializing in constitutional law and international legal reform.

Teuscher has served in the Utah House since 2021 and chaired the House Ethics Committee in the 2021-2022 and 2023-2024 sessions, while also serving on the Political Subdivisions Committee, according to Ballotpedia.
In his 2020 survey he named limited government and local control, and responsible growth, infrastructure and transportation, among his campaign priorities.
